The District of Columbia contains one tracked data center facility, CoreSite DC1, with 22,000 square feet of space and zero megawatts of total capacity recorded in this dataset.

A 22,000-square-foot footprint is modest by industry standards, and the absence of a megawatt figure means this data does not support any inference about how much compute the facility can host or power. Square footage alone tells you about the building envelope, not about the density of equipment inside or the electrical infrastructure behind it.

The dataset covers one operator in one jurisdiction and does not indicate whether other facilities exist in DC but are untracked, or whether this reflects genuine scarcity of data center infrastructure in the district. For a geography where federal demand for computing is significant, a single entry with no power figure leaves the most consequential questions unanswered.
